then.text: Spring, and the lapwings are tumbling over the field. Thank you for the lease. It sounds like a school playground.
Summer, and look at it. Bog cotton, birch scrub, a lake where there was a pit. Thank you, truly.
Autumn. The whooper swans will be in soon, up from Iceland. They always know before we do.

else.text: Winter. The birds come in their thousands to the new wetlands. Thank you for giving them the room.

cb_cutter.text: I cut turf by hand every spring, the old way, for the home fire. Nobody minds that. It's the machines that took the lot.
Is it true you can't make a decent fire with a birch? You can. It's a different fire, that's all.

c_sodling.text: It heaves itself out of the cutaway like a dropped clod and looks around sadly.

c_crexling.text: A rasping call comes from somewhere in the grass, and it is, annoyingly, this one.
